qs.q: A bookstore has customer comments from each shop location. Find the most common comment across all locations, ignoring duplicates from the same location.
Given a list of workshops, return the largest number of classes hosted in total across any run of consecutive years that each had at least one workshop.
Given meetings with a start time, an end time and a number of people, find the most people that were in a meeting at once.
Given an array of book prices and a budget, find the maximum number of unique books you can buy.
Given employee, department and salary data stored in a dictionary, find the second-highest salary in each department.
Write a function that reads and processes a CSV file, and handles the case where the file is not found.
Given a stream of Uber ride requests, count the requests in every 15-minute tumbling window.
Given a dictionary of users and their values, find the values that only the current user has and no other user has.
Given user view times as (start, end) tuples that may overlap, find the unique time ranges viewed.
Take a single-threaded solution, turn it into a Spark job, then into a real-time streaming version, and explain the trade-offs at each step.
Traverse a hierarchy in Python (depth-first search).
Course Schedule I and II (topological sort), and a problem combining merge intervals with binary search.
Using a users_viewership table, design an algorithm for the view count of each movie (merge-intervals logic).
Solve a hard LeetCode problem (BFS plus dynamic programming) in Python in 25 minutes.
House Robber II and binary tree serialize/deserialize. Solve each in SQL first, then write the equivalent Python.
Merge two sorted arrays. Then: find the smallest missing positive integer.
A variant of merge intervals. Follow-up: how would you solve it at scale?
Compute shipping cost with tiered pricing. Then: compute transaction fees from a CSV string.
Build a web crawler. Follow-up: make it multithreaded, using thread pool executors and asyncio.
Build an encoder and decoder using RLE and BP.
Write an iterator for a set that can return a snapshot of the set at any point in time.
Design a log writer that is multi-threaded but keeps the writes in order.
In a distributed N-ary tree where nodes talk only by async messages, count the nodes and print the result at the root.
Calculate the percentage of total sales completed on the same day the customer registered.
Find customers who bought 3 or more books on both the first and last day of sales, excluding those with only one transaction.
Find the top 5 customers, ordered by the average payment per book made by the people they invited.
Follow-up on your answer: how would you write it without a CTE?
Find the number of people who checked out a book on the same day that another person returned that same book.
Car rental schema: daily rental utilisation by city and car size, compared against inventory.
Rewrite your query to minimise table scans.
How long did each user stay on a page? (LEAD, then a difference.)
Find super users: users with impressions on 7 consecutive days. Then: top N, and how do you handle ties?
Find super hosts: at least three listings, an average rating above a threshold, and at least 90% of listings with a review in the last 30 days.
Find the median price for each city.
Find drivers who haven't taken a trip in the first 7 days after signup. Then: how would you optimise it as the data grows?
Find the top 3 cities each month.
Find the total time each driver spent driving each day, when a trip's start and end can fall on different days.
A hard SQL problem with window functions. Then: how would you solve it without window functions?
Find users who changed their city more than 3 times in the last year.
Print the distinct pairs of connected cities, where a→b and b→a count once.
Implement row_number() without using window functions.
Live SQL: find users with consecutive logins.
Netflix is launching an ad-supported plan and your team builds the ad system. Design the data models that let ad operations and business teams traffic direct-sold demand into the system.
Design a model for cumulative booking metrics that also shows first and last booking times. Then defend every design choice, and optimise the queries and tables.
Reels case: model the entities for feed content and shares.
Follow-ups on your model: what if I want to track changes to this? Is it one-to-many or many-to-many? How do you handle a many-to-many relationship?
Design a data model for an Uber ride app. How would you optimise the transactional table once it grows beyond 1 TB? Round-robin or hash partitioning?
Extend the model to answer new business questions. Design physical tables that handle big data at scale, then optimise them for the key analytical questions.
Build a data model for an app you use every day, then answer a set of SQL queries on it. (Graded on whether the queries are easy or complex on your model; bridge tables and SCD came up.)
For a top-10-movies report, design the remaining source tables and the warehouse tables (facts and dimensions).
An orders and transactions schema with facts and dimensions, handling Prime status as a slowly changing dimension. A clickstream and session schema, with partitions and sort keys.
Design an experimentation (A/B testing) platform, and build the data pipeline for it.
Design a key-value store.
Design config rollout and click aggregation.
Design a pipeline for Netflix clickstream events, feeding an hourly dashboard of the top trending movies in each location.
Design the backend of a near-real-time dashboard that shows the trending dishes in a city.
Design a system that returns the top 10 products.
ETL design: how do you handle messy or late data, retries and idempotency? When do you choose streaming over batch?
Walk through the steps data takes from capture to the end, and how you'd optimise the queries and tables along the way.
Build a payment system for an online game platform, covering refunds, credits and in-game items. Then: concurrent transactions, and how failure recovery works.
Here is a design on the screen. Walk the end-to-end flow, critique it, and tell us what you would change.
Infra-heavy design with the maths done out loud: throughput, latency, data size, TPS.
Design an S3-like object store. Design a distributed job scheduler like Airflow. Design a messaging system like Kafka.
Design a distributed task scheduler.
Design a system that ingests data for both product and warehousing uses, and explain how you make it resilient. Then: describe a RAG pipeline.
How would you evaluate short video's impact on the news feed? (Users, content, interactions.)
How would you measure monetization for a gaming company's product, what reports would you build, and how would you verify that a broken feature was actually fixed?
A metric drops on the dashboard of an Instagram-like product. What do you do? Should this metric be on the dashboard while you do the root-cause analysis?
Define the success metrics for a project (Lyft, Twitter or video theme).
Define the KPIs you'd track for a ride-share algorithm.
Define a success metric. The metric drops: find the root cause. What is the leading metric? What segments would you look at?
Design visualizations for streaming metrics.
Product sense in the phone screen: pick the metrics, then design the ETL (facts and dimensions) behind them.
Describe building and improving a dashboard.
Walk me through your most impactful project. (Manager round, with a domain deep dive and a Spark deep dive.)
Give a presentation of one of your previous projects (domain deep dive).
Present a recent large project end to end. How many people were involved? Can we go deeper on the GDPR data management part?
Go deeper on each of the last three companies on your resume. What changed because of your work?
Talk through your technical projects: their scale, complexity, and the decisions and trade-offs you made.
Walk through the details of an end-to-end project.
Tell me about the best projects you've worked on, or the achievements you're proudest of.
Explain the impact of your project, how you mentor, and how you split work and assign credit on a team. (The candidate was rejected because the impact 'wasn't big enough'.)
qs.who: Meta · Senior+ DE leadership round (IC6 target)

qs.q: Tell me about a time you had a conflict and made a data-driven decision.
Tell me about a conflict with your team lead or manager. A process you improved that had business impact. A time you learned a tool quickly and delivered.

Tell me about a project where a stakeholder changed priority after work had started. What would you do about a feature that is profitable for the company but clearly costs customers more money? Tell me about a bug or mistake you shipped.
What is your view on AI safety? (Recruiter call: 'develop a strong opinion'.)
Tell me about a time you led a difficult project. How did you handle conflict with a teammate? Which part of your work are you most proud of?
Leadership Principles in every screen. Prepare Dive Deep (debugging a critical pipeline under pressure) and Insist on the Highest Standards (raising data quality when deadlines were tight).
Talk about projects where you involved many teams or got leadership buy-in, and how you led and mentored others.

qs.q: How will Spark behave when you join an X GB dataset with a Y GB dataset and don't have enough resources? What can go wrong, and how would you optimise it?
Explain the physical join types: hash join and broadcast nested loop join. Then: idempotency, and change data capture (CDC).
Design pipelines, then debug scenarios on them.
Query and table optimisation questions, asked without context.
Unit and integration testing for ETL, performance tuning, and speed versus memory trade-offs in big data processing.
An AI debugging round, alongside full-stack and behavioral rounds.
